outcomes.title: I open the link and the Snake game is right there
criteria: Opening the deployed link serves the game to anyone, with no install, account or login
The page names the game as Snake
The play area is on screen, with a run ready to start straight away or one obvious control to begin

outcomes.title: When a run starts, the snake moves by itself and my score reads zero
criteria: Starting a run puts a snake on the board that moves on its own, with no key held
My score is on screen from the first moment of play, starting at zero and reading exactly "Score 0"
The run plays with no error message or frozen board

outcomes.title: My arrow keys steer the snake
criteria: The snake moves on its own, and my arrow keys turn it: Up, Down, Left and Right each steer the snake that way
I can play the whole game with the keyboard alone, with no account or extra setup
Steering never leaves the game stuck or erroring

outcomes.title: Eating food makes my snake longer and my score go up
criteria: Food appears on the board where my steering can reach it
Eating a piece of food makes the snake visibly longer
Eating adds 1 to my score: the first piece reads exactly "Score 1", the next "Score 2", and so on

outcomes.title: When I hit the wall my run ends with my result, and one action replays
criteria: Steering my snake into the wall ends the run by itself, with a game over message naming my final score
No hang and no error: the ended run settles on its result
One obvious action, such as Play again, starts a fresh run immediately, back at exactly "Score 0", without reloading the page

outcomes.title: The snake biting its own tail ends the run too
criteria: Once the snake has grown long enough, steering its head into its own body ends the run
Self-collision ends the run with the same kind of game over message naming my final score that hitting the wall shows

outcomes.title: The snake moves at a pace I can comfortably steer, right out of the box
criteria: Starting a run, the snake advances at a calm, even pace with each step clearly followable — not a blur rushing across the board
In the 3D first-person view I have time between steps to spot what is ahead and turn before hitting a wall or reaching food
This comfortable pace is what I get by default the moment a run starts, with no settings or setup needed

outcomes.title: There is a speed control in the game that I can see and use
criteria: The on-screen HUD shows a speed control offering Slow, Normal and Fast
The control names the speed currently in effect, starting at Normal
I can use it while a run is in progress, without reloading the page and without the run ending or breaking

outcomes.title: Choosing Slow, Normal or Fast really changes how fast the snake goes
criteria: Slow makes the snake noticeably slower than Normal — a careful, deliberate pace for tight steering
Fast makes it noticeably quicker than Normal for a livelier game
Normal sits between the two, and the control shows which speed is active as I switch
Steering, food and scoring still work the same way at every speed

outcomes.title: The speed I pick stays with me while I play
criteria: The snake keeps the pace I chose until I change it — it never drifts back on its own
Switching speed in the middle of a run does not freeze, restart or error anything; play simply continues at the new pace
I can play a full stretch of the game — steering, eating food, near misses — at whichever speed I picked, with scoring working as usual
